title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Clearance of Cases Involving Extended Detention
keywords_en: Court's handling of cases involving overdue detention
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issues Concerning the Clearance of Cases Involving Detention Beyond Statutory Time Limits

Fa [2003] No. 129

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Since the implementation of the revised Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in 1996, and particularly after the National People's Congress Internal Affairs and Judicial Committee conducted a major enforcement inspection of the Criminal Procedure Law in 2000, people's courts at all levels across the country have been adjudicating cases in accordance with the trial time limits prescribed by the Criminal Procedure Law. The proportion of cases concluded within the trial time limit has further increased, and a number of cases involving prolonged detention beyond the statutory time limit have been resolved. However, in some localities, the phenomenon of detention beyond the statutory time limit still exists to varying degrees, with some cases even "newly arising while old ones are being cleared." In order to effectively address the problem of detention beyond the statutory time limit existing at the trial stage of people's courts, the following notice is hereby issued:

I. Further Raise Awareness and Attach High Importance to the Problem of Detention Beyond Statutory Time Limits

Detention beyond the statutory time limit infringes upon the legitimate rights and interests of the defendant, damages the image of the people's courts and the State, and does not conform to the requirements of the people's courts' work theme of "justice and efficiency." People's courts at all levels must further raise their awareness, change the mindset of "emphasizing substance over procedure," and establish a concept that attaches equal importance to both substance and procedure. In particular, they must recognize that, as the national judicial organs, people's courts must strictly enforce the law and effectively ensure that law enforcement does not violate the law. People's courts at all levels must attach high importance to the problem of detention beyond statutory time limits, deeply understand its harmful nature, recognize the importance and urgency of solving this problem, strictly implement the relevant provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law, and effectively protect the legitimate rights and interests of the defendant.

II. Actively Take Effective Measures and Make Great Efforts to Clear Cases Involving Detention Beyond Statutory Time Limits

Each Higher People's Court must conduct a comprehensive and detailed case-by-case statistical count of the cases and individuals subject to detention beyond the statutory time limit within its jurisdiction, carefully analyze the causes of such detention, immediately adopt effective measures, and promptly proceed with the clearance. The statistical data shall be reported to the Supreme People's Court before August 20, 2003. Concealing, falsely reporting, or omitting reports is strictly prohibited. Each Higher People's Court shall designate a specific institution and personnel responsible for supervising the clearance of cases involving detention beyond the statutory time limit. In particular, cases where the detention has exceeded the statutory time limit by three years or more must be cleared by the end of 2003; cases where the detention has exceeded the statutory time limit by one year or more must be cleared by the end of September 2004. Where coordination with public security organs or people's procuratorates is necessary, communication and consultation shall be proactively strengthened. Where necessary, the local Political and Legal Affairs Committee shall be requested to coordinate and resolve the matter. After the clearance of cases involving detention beyond the statutory time limit is completed, each Higher People's Court shall promptly submit a written report on the clearance situation to the Supreme People's Court.

III. Strictly Implement the Trial Time Limit System and Strengthen Inspection and Supervision

In the process of criminal trials, people's courts at all levels must strictly implement the trial time limit system and strengthen the inspection and supervision of the enforcement of the defendant's detention period. Where circumstances that are not counted toward the trial time limit as prescribed by law, such as adjournment of trial, suspension of trial, or psychiatric evaluation, occur during the trial process, or where compulsory measures are changed according to law, the defendant, defense counsel, detention center, and other relevant departments shall be promptly notified, so as to effectively safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of the defendant.

In the near future, our Court, the National People's Congress Internal Affairs and Judicial Committee, and other departments will conduct a special inspection of the problem of detention beyond statutory time limits in people's courts. Each Higher People's Court must strictly follow the requirements of this notice, immediately commence relevant work, and prepare for the report. At the same time, on the basis of carefully analyzing the causes of the problem of detention beyond statutory time limits, propose effective countermeasures or suggestions to effectively resolve the problem of detention beyond statutory time limits arising in trials.

July 29, 2003
